questions.question: Slippery surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no other vehicles are nearby.
Are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are at high risk. Always use turn signals when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby. This helps protect you.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Leave extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than normal.
When you want to see the scenery.
To make other drivers cut you off.
To hide that you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than normal.
questions.explanation: Leave more space when the road is slippery, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Your motorcycle needs more room to stop in these situations.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of these except:
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: When borrowing a motorcycle:

options.text: It will handle the same as your own motorcycle.
The owner already checked the brakes for you.
Leave extra space and ride slowly to give yourself time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space and ride slowly to give yourself time to react.
questions.explanation: Do the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you do on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and leave yourself extra stopping distance.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in the front and rear
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in the front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: A helmet gives the best protection when:

options.text: It has only a few cracks

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers can keep you awake, but they cannot reduce your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: Check your motorcycle before riding:
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. This takes just a few minutes and helps avoid dangerous situations before you enter traffic.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you do not have to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is recommended.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator be more visible?

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead very closely.

questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Always use your headlight. Use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to move side to side. This is usually safe. Just stay relaxed and keep a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the motion, as this is dangerous and keeps you from staying in your lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. Keep more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have alcohol in your system.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have alcohol in your system.
questions.explanation: Your body can process about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair you?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you think about?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has many benefits. Most importantly, make sure other drivers can see you and you have enough space around you.

questions.question: What helps reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Blend in and don't be noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure other drivers can see you. Use turn signals, brake lights, and good lane position. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to act if danger appears.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes work best for riding?

options.text: Shoes that cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent brakes from activating if the roadway is dry.
Warn you when your brake pad needs replacing.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. It works by releasing and re-applying brake pressure when sensors detect a wheel is about to lock. This helps you stop safely and keep control.

questions.question: A person with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should be pointed downward.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag your feet on the ground or point your toes down, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Your primary source for information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate it, care for it, and maintain it.
